The candidate drops line 9 from the zero guard, which gives the same amount (when line 2 is zero the smaller of line 2 and line 12 is zero). Completed (28, all enumerated): 26 classm.s2.2 and 24 of its partials (joint, eligible all year, family coverage 10 months and on December 1, last_month No, equal division), $4,279.17 vs $4,275.00; 2 stage13.hsa_part_year_family (joint, eligible all year, family coverage 6 months and on December 1, last_month No; its fixture asserts line 6 $4,287.50), $4,287.50 vs $4,275.00; each is the line 6 difference passed through line 12.

Ruling: model error; inherited from the candidate's line 6 (through lines 8 and 12). i8889 p. 8, Line 13: "Generally, enter the smaller of line 2 or line 12 on line 13". executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/f8889.json`; 1,373 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 615 partial records from 40 bases; 1,549 comparisons): 1,399 of 1,549 agree; 20 value (1 completed), 48 candidate-refuses (13 completed), 35 project-refuses (none completed), 1 candidate-unknown (none completed), 46 project-unknown (none completed). The candidate's own line (the smaller of line 2 and line 12, zero when line 2 is zero) gives the project's amount. Completed: witness 23, the partial of classm.s2.2.deepseek withholding f8889.allocated, project $4,279.17, candidate $4,987.50 (line 6 Step 4; see line 6). The 13 completed candidate-refuses (witnesses 1, 3) are its declared h_alloc_bad (allocated more than its Step 1) also fires when the allocation is "equal" and a fixture supplies f8889.allocated anyway (classm.f8889.1.deepseek, $5,428.00 and $3,122.00; classm.s2.2[.deepseek], $8,550.00). The interview asks f8889.allocated only under "agreed" (the project reads it only there), and with it withheld the check stays silent (when_known), so these records are not ones the interview produces; under "agreed" the check is the project's cited f8889.allocation_bad ("more than the Step 1 limit allocated in total"). Refused: value through Step 4 and the spouse rule (witnesses 0, 5, 7, 8, 14); 35 project-refuses on the cited f8889.mfs, f8889.bad_months and f8889.allocation_bad (scope); the project-unknown are partial records withholding line 9 or a line 3 answer, asked of every Form 8889. Project stands.

Ruling: interface gap; i8889 p.8 line13 generally takes the smaller of contributions and remaining limit. With zero personal and employer contributions the project returns zero without computing unavailable limit inputs; the reply still demands the limit. Complete question wording does not establish answer availability. Add source-based HSA partial-input cases before qualification; no general equivalence or model-only-noise claim.

Ruling: scope; Form 8889 (2025), line 14b: "Distributions included on line 14a that you rolled over to another HSA. Also include any excess contributions (and the earnings on those excess contributions) included on line 14a that were withdrawn by the due date of your return". executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/f8889.json`; 1,373 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 615 partial records from 40 bases; 1,549 comparisons): 1,494 of 1,549 agree; 12 candidate-refuses (none completed), 43 candidate-unknown (none completed). Both enter the rollover answer, zero with no distributions, and refuse a rollover above line 14a (candidate h_rollover_bad, project f8889.rollover_bad). The 12 candidate-refuses are its declared f8889.unsupported, all on returns the project refuses on f8889.unsupported at lines 13 and 16 (witnesses 0-5, for example stage21.refuse.hsa_excess_withdrawn); the 43 candidate-unknown are partial records withholding f8889.unsupported, asked of every Form 8889. Withdrawn excess contributions are refused by f8889.unsupported on both sides. Project stands.

Ruling: interface gap; i8889 p.8 line14b counts distributions rolled over, which must be zero if total distributions are zero. The reply requires an absent rollover answer; the diagnostic source witness also finds that the project unconditional rollover_bad refusal gate demands that same answer before its zero branch (BUG-0138). Both need correction/validation; no passing review or clean model-only finding.

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. The project floors the subtraction at zero; line 14b is at most line 14a (f8889.rollover_bad refuses otherwise), so the floor never applies and the value is f8889 line 14c, "Subtract line 14b from line 14a".

Ruling: scope; i8889 p. 8, Line 15: "Only include on line 15 distributions from your HSA that were used to pay you for qualified medical expenses not reimbursed by insurance or other coverage". executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/f8889.json`; 1,373 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 615 partial records from 40 bases; 1,549 comparisons): 1,536 of 1,549 agree; 13 candidate-refuses (none completed). All 13 are candidate refusals on refused returns, inherited from its line 14b (f8889.unsupported; witness 3 stage16.refuse.f8889.rollover_over, its h_rollover_bad where the project refuses on f8889.rollover_bad). Otherwise both enter the medical answer, zero with no distributions. The candidate also refuses a medical answer above line 14c (h_medical_bad), which the project's question does not admit: it asks for the part of the 2025 HSA distributions used for qualified medical expenses, and a rolled-over distribution cannot be one; line 16 floors at zero either way. Project stands.

Ruling: interface gap; i8889 p.8 line15 includes only distributed dollars used for qualified medical expenses. When line14a is zero, no medical follow-up is needed. The reply requires that answer, unlike the authored zero branch. The diagnostic source witness confirms the missing-input difference; no HSA case bank was present in this request and no whole-form equivalence is claimed.

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. The project enters zero when line 16 is zero; then the second's amount is 20% of zero either way, since the part subject to the tax is at most line 16 (f8889.subject_bad refuses otherwise; i8889 p. 9, "Enter on line 17b only 20% (0.20) of any amount included on line 16 that does not meet any of the exceptions"). rulings.ruling: Ruling: ambiguity and model error; i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 4: "If you were, or were considered, an eligible individual for the entire year and you changed your type of coverage during the year, enter on line 3 (see (6) in this list) the greater of: a. The limitation shown on the last line of the Line 3 Limitation Chart and Worksheet (in these instructions), or b. The maximum amount that can be contributed based on the type of HDHP coverage you had on the first day of the last month of your tax year"; i8889 p. 5, Line 3, Note: "If you are married and had family coverage at any time during the year, the additional contribution amount is figured on line 7 and is not included on line 3". executable-triage-v2 (`../triage/f8889.json`; 1,372 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 615 partial records from 40 bases; 1,548 comparisons): 1,516 of 1,548 agree; 20 value (19 refused, 1 incomplete), 9 candidate-unknown, 2 project-unknown, 1 candidate-refuses; no completed return has a value difference. (1) Under the last-month rule the candidate always takes the December 1 maximum (rule 2); the project applies rule 4's greater-of when the coverage type changed, the owner's ruling amb.2025.hsa_last_month_change (witnesses 0 and 2 classm.f8889.4[.deepseek], refused: project $5,716.67, candidate $4,300.00; witness 4 stage11.hsa.last_month_changed, incomplete: $5,358.33 against $4,300.00). (2) The candidate puts the $1,000 additional amount in line 3 for the self-only months of a married filer who had family coverage in other months, which the Note forbids (witness 6 generated 154: married filing jointly, age 55, eligible all year, one family month, December self-only, last-month rule not used: project $4,654.17 = (11 × $4,300 + $8,550) / 12, candidate $5,570.83 with $5,300 a self-only month); the candidate pairs it with family months on line 7 ($83.33 against $1,000.00), so line 8 differs only by a cent (model error on the Note; line 7 is amb.2025.hsa_line7_months). (3) It reads "married" from the filing status (witness 1 classm.f8959.2 and witness 5 generated 128: married filing separately with household.married false, refused on f8889.mfs; scope). Witness 3 stage11.refuse.hsa_months: the candidate's declared h_months_bad where the project refuses on its cited gate f8889.bad_months (scope). The unknowns are partial records; on the 2 completed ones (witness 13 classm.s3.3.deepseek) the candidate needs f8889.last_month where December coverage is family, which the source does not need (rule 2 and rule 4 then both give $8,550), though the interview asks it. Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: ambiguity and model error; i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 4: "If you were, or were considered, an eligible individual for the entire year and you changed your type of coverage during the year, enter on line 3 (see (6) in this list) the greater of: a. The limitation shown on the last line of the Line 3 Limitation Chart and Worksheet (in these instructions), or b. The maximum amount that can be contributed based on the type of HDHP coverage you had on the first day of the last month of your tax year"; i8889 p. 5, Line 3, Note: "If you are married and had family coverage at any time during the year, the additional contribution amount is figured on line 7 and is not included on line 3". Two differences. (1) The candidate applies rule 2 (the December 1 maximum) to every last-month-rule filer; the project applies rule 4's greater-of when the coverage type changed, the owner's ruling amb.2025.hsa_last_month_change (keep rule 4). Witnesses 0 and 2 classm.f8889.4[.deepseek] (refused; last-month rule, December self-only, 4 family months): project $5,716.67, candidate $4,300.00; witness 4 stage11.hsa.last_month_changed (incomplete): $5,358.33 against $4,300.00. (2) The candidate reads "married" from the filing status; the project from the marital answer (household.married), as the instructions use the word "married", not a filing status: witness 5 audit.f8889.married_hoh_family_age55 (married, head of household; incomplete): project $8,550.00 with $1,000.00 on line 7, candidate $9,550.00 with $0.00, the same line 8 (model error). executable-triage-v2 (`../triage/f8889.json`; 1,372 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 615 partial records from 40 bases; 1,548 comparisons): 1,517 of 1,548 agree; 20 value (18 refused, 2 incomplete), 6 candidate-unknown (2 on completed returns, partial records of classm.s3.3.deepseek withholding f8889.last_month, which the project does not need when December coverage is family: rule 4's greater-of is then the $8,550 maximum either way), 5 project-unknown on partial records. Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Both apply rules 1 to 6 of Line 3 (i8889 pp. 4-5) with the page 5 Note that a married filer with family coverage at any time figures the additional contribution amount on line 7: the second leaves the $1,000 out of the family amount for any married filer and out of the self-only amount when married with family coverage, the project out of both when married with family coverage. A married filer without family coverage has no family months, so the family amount is not read; the values agree.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained (as the prior rulings). (1) The project leaves the $1,000 additional contribution amount off line 3 for a married filer treated as having family coverage at any time, as rule 6 (i8889 p. 4, 'age 55 or older and unmarried or married with self-only HDHP coverage for the entire year') and the page 5 Note ('If you are married and had family coverage at any time during the year, the additional contribution amount is figured on line 7 and is not included on line 3') say; the second puts it on line 3 for every filer. (2) Under the last-month rule with a change of coverage the project applies rule 4, the owner's ruling (amb.2025.hsa_last_month_change). The marital test now reads household.married, the filer's answer, as the instructions' word is 'married', not a filing status.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Two differences remain. (1) The second puts the $5,300 self-only amount for age 55 or older on line 3 for every filer; the project leaves out the $1,000 for a married filer treated as having family coverage at any time, as rule 6 ("age 55 or older and unmarried or married with self-only HDHP coverage for the entire year, you can increase the amount ... by $1,000", i8889 p. 4) and the Note (p. 5, "If you are married and had family coverage at any time during the year, the additional contribution amount is figured on line 7 and is not included on line 3") require; the chart's unqualified self-only box (p. 6) is read with that Note, and the second's reading would count the $1,000 again on line 7. (2) The second takes rule 4's greater-of for every filer eligible all twelve months, the project only when the coverage type changed; when it did not change, the December 1 maximum is the chart amount, so the values agree. The second now applies rule 4 to a last-month-rule filer as the project does (amb.2025.hsa_last_month_change, owner ruling), so the earlier split on that reading is gone; married filing separately is refused (f8889.mfs).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. As ruled before: (1) the project leaves the $1,000 additional contribution amount off line 3 for a married filer treated as having family coverage at any time, as rule 6 (i8889 p. 4, "age 55 or older and unmarried or married with self-only HDHP coverage for the entire year, you can increase the amount ... by $1,000") and the Note (p. 5, "If you are married and had family coverage at any time during the year, the additional contribution amount is figured on line 7 and is not included on line 3") require; (2) rule 4's greater-of agrees in value when the coverage type did not change. The new difference is the last-month rule for a filer eligible all twelve months, the owner's ruling amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year (reading 1, i8889 p. 4, rule 2). Medicare months are excluded from the eligible months by the question, as the second's note assumes; married filing separately is refused (f8889.mfs).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error and scope; i8889 p. 7, Line 6, Step 4: "Determine any other contribution limits that apply for the tax year and add that amount to the result in Step 3. Enter the total on line 6"; i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 4: "If you were, or were considered, an eligible individual for the entire year and you changed your type of coverage during the year, enter on line 3 (see (6) in this list) the greater of: a. The limitation shown on the last line of the Line 3 Limitation Chart and Worksheet (in these instructions), or b. The maximum amount that can be contributed based on the type of HDHP coverage you had on the first day of the last month of your tax year", and its TIP, "If you had family coverage on the first day of the last month, you do not need to use the worksheet; enter $8,550 on line 3". executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/f8889.json`; 1,373 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 615 partial records from 40 bases; 1,549 comparisons): 1,387 of 1,549 agree; 34 value (3 completed), 63 candidate-refuses (13 completed), 13 project-refuses (none completed), 47 candidate-unknown (none completed), 5 project-unknown (none completed). (1) Step 4: the candidate takes Step 4 as line 5 less Step 1, the project as the self-only monthly amount of each eligible month without family coverage. They part where rule 4 raises line 3 above the worksheet. Witness: the partial of classm.s2.2.deepseek that withholds f8889.allocated, a completed return and the record the interview produces under "equal" (joint; taxpayer eligible 12 months, family coverage 10 months and on December 1, last-month rule not used, under 55). Line 3 is $8,550.00 on both (the rule 4 TIP); Step 1 $7,125.00; Step 3 $3,562.50. The project adds $716.67 (2 × $4,300 / 12) for line 6 $4,279.17; the candidate adds $1,425.00 for $4,987.50. The extra $708.33 is the amount by which rule 4 raises the $7,841.67 worksheet total to the December 1 family maximum. That is family-coverage limit, which the spouse rule divides (Step 2; p969 p. 6, "If either spouse has family HDHP coverage, both spouses are treated as having family HDHP coverage. ... the contribution limit is split equally between the spouses unless you agree on a different division"), not an "other contribution limit". The project's $4,279.17 is also the greater of rule 4's two amounts after the division ($3,562.50 + $716.67 against $8,550.00 / 2 = $4,275.00). The candidate's reading is not in the register. The 3 completed value differences are this record and its twin; the refused witnesses 0, 1 and 10 (classm.f8889.2[.deepseek], December family coverage after self-only months: project $4,281.25, candidate $5,343.75) are the same mechanism. (2) The 13 completed candidate-refuses (witnesses 2, 5) are its declared h_alloc_bad (allocated more than its Step 1) also fires when the allocation is "equal" and a fixture supplies f8889.allocated anyway (classm.f8889.1.deepseek, $5,428.00 and $3,122.00; classm.s2.2[.deepseek], $8,550.00). The interview asks f8889.allocated only under "agreed" (the project reads it only there), and with it withheld the check stays silent (when_known), so these records are not ones the interview produces; under "agreed" the check is the project's cited f8889.allocation_bad ("more than the Step 1 limit allocated in total"). (3) The spouse rule on joint returns answering household.married false (witnesses 7, 9: $2,850.00 against $1,425.00), married filing separately (witness 4) and the candidate's f8889.unsupported, all on refused returns; the project-refuses are its cited f8889.allocation_bad (witnesses 12-17): scope. Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: owner ruling (register entry amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year, reading 1, accepted 2026-10-22); project retained. The second applies the last-month rule only to a filer not eligible in all twelve months; the project applies it to any filer eligible on December 1 who answers that they use it, as i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, "You may consider yourself an 'eligible individual' for the entire year if you are an eligible individual on the 1st day of the last month", and p. 4, Line 3, rule 2, "You are treated as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month of your tax year"; the owner chose this reading. The second's note that the spouses' allocations are not checked against each other: they are, by f8889.allocation_bad, which refuses when only one spouse's Form 8889 uses the rule or an agreed allocation, when the two Step 1 limits differ, or when the agreed shares add up to more than the Step 1 limit (i8889 p. 7, Line 6, Step 2, "unless you both agree on a different allocation").

rulings.ruling: Ruling: genuine ambiguity (register entry amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year, proposed for the owner); project retained pending the owner. This second transcription applies the last-month rule only to a filer who was not an eligible individual in all twelve months (months eligible under 12); the project applies it to any filer eligible on December 1 who answers that they use it. The text supports both: the rule is open to anyone eligible on December 1 (i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, "You may consider yourself an 'eligible individual' for the entire year if you are an eligible individual on the 1st day of the last month") and treats such a filer "as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month" (i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 2), and p969 p. 6, Example 2 calls the $8,550 of a filer covered all year (self-only, then family from November 1) a contribution made under the last-month rule; but rules 3 and 4 separate a filer who "were" from one who "were considered" eligible for the entire year (i8889 p. 4), and p969 p. 5 limits the same-coverage treatment to months "if you didn't otherwise have coverage". The readings differ only for a filer eligible all year who changed coverage type and answers yes (through Step 1 and the spouse-rule test, as ruled on f8889.step1 and f8889.split). Two further differences, both project retained: the second's Step 4 adds the $1,000 additional contribution amount to each self-only month of a married filer age 55 or older, which the project leaves to line 7 (i8889 p. 5, Note, "If you are married and had family coverage at any time during the year, the additional contribution amount is figured on line 7 and is not included on line 3"), and line 7 counts every eligible month under the owner-accepted reading amb.2025.hsa_line7_months, so adding it in Step 4 as well would count it twice; and with family coverage every month the steps reduce to the first bullet, as ruled before (i8889 p. 7, Line 6).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: genuine ambiguity (register entry amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year, proposed for the owner); project retained pending the owner. This second transcription applies the last-month rule only to a filer who was not an eligible individual in all twelve months (months eligible under 12); the project applies it to any filer eligible on December 1 who answers that they use it. The text supports both: the rule is open to anyone eligible on December 1 (i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, "You may consider yourself an 'eligible individual' for the entire year if you are an eligible individual on the 1st day of the last month") and treats such a filer "as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month" (i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 2), and p969 p. 6, Example 2 calls the $8,550 of a filer covered all year (self-only, then family from November 1) a contribution made under the last-month rule; but rules 3 and 4 separate a filer who "were" from one who "were considered" eligible for the entire year (i8889 p. 4), and p969 p. 5 limits the same-coverage treatment to months "if you didn't otherwise have coverage". The readings differ only for a filer eligible all year who changed coverage type and answers yes (through the family-coverage test and the month count). The rest is the recorded reading amb.2025.hsa_line7_months (owner accepted after Stage 13), binding: the second counts only months treated as having family coverage, the project every month treated as eligible (i8889 p. 7, Additional Contribution Amount Worksheet, "$1,000 x number of months eligible", and "If items (1) and (2) apply to all months during 2025, enter $1,000"). Filing status: the second also allows married filing separately, which is refused (f8889.mfs).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: genuine ambiguity (register entry amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year, proposed for the owner); project retained pending the owner. This second transcription applies the last-month rule only to a filer who was not an eligible individual in all twelve months (months eligible under 12); the project applies it to any filer eligible on December 1 who answers that they use it. The text supports both: the rule is open to anyone eligible on December 1 (i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, "You may consider yourself an 'eligible individual' for the entire year if you are an eligible individual on the 1st day of the last month") and treats such a filer "as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month" (i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 2), and p969 p. 6, Example 2 calls the $8,550 of a filer covered all year (self-only, then family from November 1) a contribution made under the last-month rule; but rules 3 and 4 separate a filer who "were" from one who "were considered" eligible for the entire year (i8889 p. 4), and p969 p. 5 limits the same-coverage treatment to months "if you didn't otherwise have coverage". The readings differ only for a filer eligible all year who changed coverage type and answers yes (the Step 1 amount this line halves or replaces). Otherwise as ruled before: the second figures Step 3 as Step 1 less the spouse's part, the project takes half of Step 1 or your agreed part directly, equal when the agreed part is at most Step 1, which both require (i8889 p. 7, Line 6, Steps 2 and 3, "Subtract the part of the contribution limit allocated to your spouse in Step 2 from the amount determined in Step 1"); halving rounds half-up to the cent (amb.2025.multiplication_subcent).

You are treated as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month of your tax year". The project refigures with the months of family coverage (or all twelve under the last-month rule, the owner's reading amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year). executable-triage-v2 (`../triage/f8889.json`; 1,372 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 615 partial records from 40 bases; 1,548 comparisons): 1,371 of 1,548 agree; 102 value (33 on completed returns), 56 candidate-unknown, 11 candidate-refuses, 8 project-unknown. The unknowns are partial records withholding the last-month answer the candidate reads; the candidate refusals are its f8889.unsupported raised on returns the project also refuses. Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: genuine ambiguity (register entry amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year, proposed for the owner); project retained pending the owner. This second transcription applies the last-month rule only to a filer who was not an eligible individual in all twelve months (months eligible under 12); the project applies it to any filer eligible on December 1 who answers that they use it. The text supports both: the rule is open to anyone eligible on December 1 (i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, "You may consider yourself an 'eligible individual' for the entire year if you are an eligible individual on the 1st day of the last month") and treats such a filer "as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month" (i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 2), and p969 p. 6, Example 2 calls the $8,550 of a filer covered all year (self-only, then family from November 1) a contribution made under the last-month rule; but rules 3 and 4 separate a filer who "were" from one who "were considered" eligible for the entire year (i8889 p. 4), and p969 p. 5 limits the same-coverage treatment to months "if you didn't otherwise have coverage". The readings differ only for a filer eligible all year who changed coverage type and answers yes; then the months "treated as having family coverage" (i8889 p. 7, Line 6, Step 1) are all twelve (December family) or none (December self-only) in the project, the actual family months in the second. The other difference is the one ruled before: the second takes the family monthly amount from its line 3 chart helper, which on a joint return (the only case in which Step 1 is read) is hsa.family, as the project uses.

Ruling: representation; project retained. Both refigure line 5 with only the months treated as having family coverage (i8889 p. 7, Line 6, Step 1). The second takes the family monthly amount from its line 3 chart helper, which for a married filer is $8,550 whatever the age (the additional contribution amount is on line 7, p. 5 Note); the project uses hsa.family directly. On a joint return, the only case in which Step 1 is read, the amounts are the same.

Ruling: owner ruling (register entry amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year, reading 1, accepted 2026-10-22); project retained. The second applies the last-month rule only to a filer not eligible in all twelve months; the project applies it to any filer eligible on December 1 who answers that they use it, as i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, "You may consider yourself an 'eligible individual' for the entire year if you are an eligible individual on the 1st day of the last month", and p. 4, Line 3, rule 2, "You are treated as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month of your tax year"; the owner chose this reading. The other difference is the one ruled before: the second takes the family monthly amount from its line 3 chart helper, which on a joint return (the only case in which Step 1 is read) is hsa.family, as the project uses; married filing separately is refused (f8889.mfs).
